narrative.overview:
This system reads like a working research document: precise, analytical, every element functional. The visual grammar is flat surfaces, ruled separations, monospace metadata, and type hierarchy that does all the lifting. No shadows. No gradients. No chrome that is not also content. The accent color is a measurement marker; it appears where something needs to be noted, not where something wants to look good.

Typography is system-native (SF Pro on Apple, Segoe on Windows) used with intent: one tight scale, two weights, one mono stack for labels. Two themes exist as fully committed alternate worlds: light is warm (hue 80 ivory), dark is cool (hue 255 near-midnight blue-black).

This system explicitly rejects startup SaaS aesthetics, developer portfolio templates with neon glows, and flashy futuristic portfolios. The correct reference is peer-reviewed confidence: the work is the proof, the format stays out of the way.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by default: depth comes from whitespace and type scale, never from shadows.
Tonal warmth via background tint (hue 80), not via warm accent colors.
Dark mode is a fully committed alternate world (cool hue 255), not a color inversion.
Live data (ORCID + GitHub APIs) means graceful skeleton states, never blank sections.
Motion is purposeful: staggered load entrance, scroll reveals, scroll-driven parallax. All disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Instrument Teal is the only accent. Never as a background for large regions, never in gradients, never at full opacity on surfaces. Its sole role is annotation: it marks something to notice. Rarity is structural.

rules.name: The Dual-World Rule
rules.body: Light and dark mode are not tonal inversions. Light is warm (hue 80); dark is cool (hue 255, near-midnight blue-black). Do not create warm dark mode variants.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow on cards or hover states. Use a 1px solid border transition instead. The only permitted blur is backdrop-filter on nav and mobile drawer, where it is structural.

rules.name: The Italic Em Rule
rules.body: Section headings (h2) often split into a weight-600 plain clause and a weight-300 italic qualifier via em. Limit to one em per heading. Do not use italic emphasis on body prose for decoration.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears only on data-derived labels: ISO years, programming language names, statistical metadata. Not on navigation, not on body prose, not on headings.

dos: Do use var(--accent) on a maximum of ~10% of any viewport's visual surface.
Do express depth via tonal surface steps (--bg → --bg-raised → --bg-float) and ruled 1px var(--line) borders.
Do use the italic em pattern on display and headline elements for qualifier clauses only.
Do restrict mono (--fm) to data-derived labels: years, language names, numeric metadata.
Do add .in directly in JavaScript when rendering dynamic ORCID or GitHub content.
Do verify WCAG AA (at least 4.5:1) for any new text color in both light and dark themes.
Do provide skeleton shimmer states for any section that loads asynchronously.
Do use transform: scaleX() (not width) for animated progress bars.
Do use opacity + visibility + pointer-events (not display:none) for drawers.
donts: Don't add box-shadow to cards, containers, or hover states.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively; backdrop-filter is structural on nav and drawer only.
Don't add numbered section markers or tiny all-caps tracked eyebrows above headings.
Don't use canvas-motif backgrounds, neon glows, scan lines, grain overlays, or particle systems.
Don't write startup SaaS copy (powerful, seamless, next-generation, cutting-edge).
Don't introduce a second accent color.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't toggle mobile nav with display:none; use opacity + visibility.
Don't make dark mode warm-tinted; dark mode uses cool hue 255.
